From 9b0cf064ea0a6bac5e1a5fb43b004fd52fbe2b3b Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Carlos Llamas <cmllamas@google.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 18:38:17 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] bpf: Switch CONFIG_CFI_CLANG to CONFIG_CFI

This was renamed in commit 23ef9d439769 ("kcfi: Rename CONFIG_CFI_CLANG
to CONFIG_CFI") as it is now a compiler-agnostic option. Using the wrong
name results in the code getting compiled out. Meaning the CFI failures
for btf_dtor_kfunc_t would still trigger.

Fixes: 99fde4d06261 ("bpf, btf: Enforce destructor kfunc type with CFI")
Signed-off-by: Carlos Llamas <cmllamas@google.com>
Reviewed-by: Sami Tolvanen <samitolvanen@google.com>
Acked-by: Yonghong Song <yonghong.song@linux.dev>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20260312183818.2721750-1-cmllamas@google.com
Signed-off-by: Alexei Starovoitov <ast@kernel.org>

diff --git a/kernel/bpf/btf.c b/kernel/bpf/btf.c
index c5876c91face..0c465f0077d5 100644
--- a/kernel/bpf/btf.c
+++ b/kernel/bpf/btf.c
@@ -9020,7 +9020,7 @@ static int btf_check_dtor_kfuncs(struct btf *btf, const struct btf_id_dtor_kfunc
 		if (!t || !btf_type_is_ptr(t))
 			return -EINVAL;
 
-		if (IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_CFI_CLANG)) {
+		if (IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_CFI)) {
 			/* Ensure the destructor kfunc type matches btf_dtor_kfunc_t */
 			t = btf_type_by_id(btf, t->type);
 			if (!btf_type_is_void(t))
-- 
2.34.1

**Summary of modifications:**

The patch applies a single change to the file `kernel/bpf/btf.c`:

- **Modified line**: In the `btf_check_dtor_kfuncs` function, the preprocessor condition `IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_CFI_CLANG)` was replaced with `IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_CFI)`.

**Reason and relationship:**  
The Linux kernel renamed the configuration option `CONFIG_CFI_CLANG` to `CONFIG_CFI` in commit `23ef9d439769` to make it compiler-agnostic. The original code in `btf.c` still used the old name, causing the CFI-based type enforcement for `btf_dtor_kfunc_t` to be compiled out when CFI was enabled. This patch updates the condition to use the new config name, restoring the intended behavior where the destructor kfunc type is validated under CFI. The fix ensures that the check introduced by commit `99fde4d06261` works correctly with the renamed config option.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
`if (IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_CFI_CLANG)) {`
Reason:
The macro `CONFIG_CFI_CLANG` was renamed to `CONFIG_CFI` in a later commit, but the code still used the old name. Since `CONFIG_CFI_CLANG` is no longer defined, `IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_CFI_CLANG)` always evaluates to false, causing the CFI type verification for `btf_dtor_kfunc_t` to be compiled out. This leaves a gap where destructor kfunc type mismatches can go undetected and trigger CFI failures at runtime.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
`if (IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_CFI)) {`
Reason:
The macro `CONFIG_CFI` is the correct, compiler-agnostic name introduced in commit 23ef9d439769. By using `IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_CFI)`, the CFI type check is properly compiled in when the kernel is built with CFI support, ensuring that destructor kfunc types are validated and preventing potential CFI failures.

The commit 99fde4d06261 introduced a CFI-based type check for destructor kfuncs using the config macro `CONFIG_CFI_CLANG`.
